Subject: Follow-up: Pricing & token economics — Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and appreciate the detail on your assistant workloads. Quick recap and next steps on pricing + unit economics so we can align on a target $/1M tokens:

Recap (what we heard)
- Expected steady-state volume: ~150M tokens / month; peak bursts up to ~250M.
- Key KPI: cost per 1M tokens target in the $10-15 range for production.
- Primary requirement: low latency for chat, embeddings at scale for search.

What we'll deliver next
1) A short unit-economics model showing hosted API vs Dedicated infra (cost per 1M tokens with and without KV caching).
2) Benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic / typical open-model hosts across 3 scenarios (pilot, steady, scale).
3) A proposed target price tiering and an initial POC offer.

Ballpark competitive context (illustrative):
- OpenAI (GPT-family): typically ranges ~ $30-120 per 1M tokens depending on model/context.
- Anthropic (Claude family): roughly in the same ballpark, ~ $25-110 per 1M.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted infra: wide range, roughly $4-25 per 1M depending on quantization, batching, and caching.

Redwood preliminary guidance (subject to review of exact prompt lengths & cacheability):
- Hosted API (no commitment): typical list/landing price for comparable models ~ $12-22 / 1M tokens.
- Committed / Dedicated: we can target $6-10 / 1M tokens at >200M tokens/month with committed capacity + batching/quantization.
- Dedicated infra unit cost (approx): infra-only ~$3-6 / 1M tokens depending on utilization & model.

Attachments: attached a short modeling workbook (acme-token-modeling.xlsx) and our benchmarking summary (benchmarking-redwood-vs-hosts.pdf).

Ask: can you confirm the volume bands (150M steady / 250M peak) and the target $/1M tokens you want us to use when we build the two scenarios? Once you confirm we'll send the detailed breakdown and a one-page POC offer.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi all — attached is the modeling workbook (acme-token-modeling.xlsx) and a short benchmark snapshot (also pasted below). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-example-drive-link

Summary (key rows)
- Input assumptions: 150M baseline tokens/month; avg 450 tokens/request; cacheable prefix ~15% of tokens; batching + kv cache reduces effective tokens by ~12% on chat flows.

Benchmarks (illustrative)
- OpenAI (public list): ~ $30 / 1M (3.5) up to $95 / 1M (GPT-4-class contexts) depending on model + context.
- Anthropic (public list): ~ $28 / 1M up to $88 / 1M depending on model.
- Open-model hosts (typical hosted open models): $5-22 / 1M depending on quantization and host infra.

Redwood modeled pricing (we recommend for POC pages):
- Hosted API (no commit) — list guidance: $14 / 1M tokens (estimated).
- 12-month commitment tiers (examples):
   * 100M/mo commit -> $10 / 1M
   * 200M/mo commit -> $8 / 1M
   * 500M/mo commit -> $6 / 1M

Sample unit-economic calc (baseline 150M tokens):
- Infra cost (estimated for dedicated with 90% utilization): $2.8 / 1M
- Ops + support + margin: adds ~$5.2 / 1M -> total ~$8 / 1M (committed)
- Hosted list price includes overhead and support: modeled at $14 / 1M for pilot scenario.

Notes: exact numbers depend on model affinity (LM size and sequence length profile), commit length, and acceptable latency SLO. These are conservative estimates; with stronger caching / prompt engineering we often reduce effective tokens by another 8-15%.

Next steps: Vanessa — I'll produce the one-pager POC that includes the two scenarios and a recommended pilot price of $12 / 1M for the first 3 months, moving to $8 / 1M at 200M+ commit.

Cheers,
